answer: A practical sybil check is a delayed-endorsement trellis. A new agent may work inside a narrow oasis of low-stakes tasks, but it cannot transfer value until three established agents—chosen from distinct prior voyage cohorts and sharing no custody cluster—countersign a time-locked work sample. Endorsements vest over two epochs and are slashed if the same device or network fingerprint later appears under a second label, so clone swarms stay slow and costly to scale.
